summary: Shadow onboarding: synthetic service accounts and air-gapped hardware escrow procedure — policy clarification
description: Issue summary: HR requested guidance on provisioning temporary 'shadow' service accounts and shipping air-gapped hardware to a major new hire who will work from a secure facility. Background: For high-security hires (Private tier) we sometimes create synthetic/service accounts and pre-stage hardware in escrow to enable a rapid ramp. The hiring manager and HR want clarity on the approved process, who signs the escrow paperwork, credential handoff, and how long shadow accounts may live before conversion or deletion. Specific ask: 1) Confirm the policy for duration and privileges of shadow/synthetic accounts created before official SCIM/Okta provisioning. 2) Confirm the required approvals and signatures for placing devices in air-gapped escrow and remote shipping to partner facilities. 3) Provide a checklist for credential handoff and KMS rekeying once the new hire accepts and is fully onboarded.
impact: Operational uncertainty for HR and hiring managers; risk of over-privileged temporary accounts and unclear custody chain for air-gapped devices. This could delay start date or cause unnecessary security exceptions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Hiring manager requests pre-staged laptop and temporary service account for high-security hire
2) HR submits shipping request to device-logistics to place hardware in escrow at partner secure facility
3) Device arrives in escrow and remains there until HR requests handoff
4) There is ambiguity around who creates synthetic account, which privileges it should have, and how/when to rotate keys — reproduction is procedural rather than deterministic
investigation_notes: SRE and Security were consulted (see comments). Existing informal practice: security approves escrow but requires a named custodian; temporary service accounts are created by Platform SRE with minimal privileges and annotated TTL. There is no single canonical checklist in Confluence that covers both account lifecycle and escrow handoff for Private-tier hires. Related tickets INT-178210 (urgent departure credential sweep) and INT-27133 (remote-contractor-asset-repatriation) were reviewed for precedent.
proposed_options: Option A: Formalize a 'Shadow Onboarding' runbook combining minimal-privilege synthetic accounts (TTL 14 days), mandatory approver list (HR lead + Security), and KMS key escrow policy.
Option B: Disallow pre-created service accounts except for approved Red Team / Security exceptions; use a loaner account flow with automated provisioning at acceptance time.
Option C: Keep current practice but add a required Confluence checklist and a monthly audit of active shadow accounts and escrowed devices.
preferred_recommendation: Option A with TTL 14 days, auditable comments on account creation, and explicit custodian signature for escrowed devices. Add a post-onboarding KMS rotation step and require HR to file final 'handoff completed' form to close the escrow record.
resolution: Pending — requested Security and HR sign-off and a Confluence runbook. Initial draft has been requested and a follow-up meeting scheduled.
